memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting." - Exod 38:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most striking verses in the chapter. The basin where priests washed was made from women's mirrors.

Bronze mirrors were valuable and personal. In a desert camp, a polished mirror may have been a woman's only way of seeing her own face. And these women handed them over.

What was once used to look at themselves became the vessel used to make others clean.

That is a beautiful picture of what happens when someone turns from self-preoccupation to service. Nothing was wasted — the material was the same bronze. Only its purpose changed.

Notice that these women "served at the entrance to the tent of meeting." They had a recognised place in the life of Israel's worship, and Scripture records their gift specifically.

We live in an age of unprecedented self-viewing. Cameras in every pocket, endless images of ourselves, constant attention to how we appear. The question this verse quietly asks is whether all that looking could be turned outward.

Paul urges us to value others above ourselves, looking not to our own interests but to the interests of others (Phil 2:3-4). Jesus, who had every right to be admired, took a towel and a basin and washed feet (John 13:5).

Mirrors can become basins.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How much of your attention goes to how you appear to others?
2. What could you redirect from self-focus to serving someone else?
3. Whose feet is God asking you to wash this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, turn my eyes away from myself. Take what I use for my own image and make it useful to others. Amen.
